approvalTitle: requirements.md: converting the Databricks diagrams to DISL and FBL
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim (2026-10-09):

> Create spec workflow MCP specifications. One specification for converting one of the standalone diagram tools to FBL and DISL. i.e. analyse the current implementation, define the DISL and FBL and then write the specification on the refactoring., also focus on finding issues and aspects where the DISL and FBL languages do not yet cover everything.

This is one of the fifteen specifications that reading gives (the series and the survey behind it are in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, *Introduction*). It converts **Databricks**: the module `src/diagrams/databricks/`, which is on neither language and holds **three tool types in one module**, all of kind diagram: the bundle (`databricks/bundle`), the job (`databricks/job`) and the pipeline (`databricks/pipeline`). One specification covers the module, because the three share one store, one set of commands and, above all, one file.

**That shared file is what this conversion is about.** The three tool types are three readings of configuration Databricks' own tooling owns: an asset bundle's `databricks.yml`, a job resource YAML, a pipeline settings file in JSON or YAML. The shipped example opens one `databricks.yml` as a bundle and, through a second registration with a `resource:` header, as a pipeline. FBL section 9 says how several readings share one body, and it is the part of FBL this tool tests hardest: finding B1 is that the rule of FBL 9.2 and the rule of FBL 5.1 cannot both be kept for this file without a construct FBL does not have.

**What "converted" means here** is what it means in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: toolbox, context menus, property rows, findings and refusals derived from bundled DISL definitions by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl`, the body read and written through an FBL binding by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl`, and module code only for what neither language can state. Nothing a user sees or a file holds changes unless this document names the change and the user has ruled on it.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: the module at `develop` `9a646009`; in etalii-adp/etalii.adp at `develop` `da64ff0` the three drafts under `definitions/diagrams/` with their companion pages, the excerpt `specifications/disl/databricks-job.dis`, the two example bindings, the DISL specification (0.3 draft) and the FBL specification (0.2 draft); and the two libraries in this repository.

| Thing | State |
| --- | --- |
| The module's backend | 4,684 lines of C# in 49 files. Three readers over YamlDotNet (`BundleParser` 190 lines, `JobParser` 175, `PipelineParser` 139) and three line-splicing writers (`BundleWriter` 150, `JobWriter` 335, `PipelineWriter` 162, with `DatabricksSplices` 97). `DatabricksRuleSet` (180) holds ten findings, `DatabricksValidator` an eleventh; `DatabricksContextActionProvider` (488), `DatabricksContextPropertyProvider` (187) and `DatabricksToolboxProvider` (69) hold menus, rows and three palettes as code. 21 test files, 11 byte-compared fixtures. |
| The module's client | 957 lines in 8 files. `DatabricksCanvas.tsx` (416) is one hand-written canvas for the three tool types; `useSimulatedRun.ts` (228) plays the mock run, deploy and update. |
| The DISL definitions | Three drafts in etalii.adp, 375, 409 and 378 lines, **all DISL 0.1**, each with `persistence.format` naming a plugin. A fourth file, `specifications/disl/databricks-job.dis` (509 lines, DISL 0.2), is the specification's own excerpt of the job and already uses constructs the draft works around. None is bundled here: `src/diagrams/databricks/definition/` does not exist. |
| The FBL bindings | Two examples in etalii.adp, vendored unchanged in `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl.Tests/Conformance/`: `databricks-job.fbl#job` and `databricks-pipeline.fbl#settings`. **No binding exists for the bundle.** The two are separate documents with separate names. |
| The real-file check | `RealFileCorpus` reads four job files and two settings files through the two bindings. `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` does not compare them with this module's parsers, as it does for the timeline and the causal loop diagram. Two divergences are recorded (finding B2). |
| A parity transcript | None. |

**How each finding is known:** *recorded* is an entry of `RealFiles/divergences.json` or a sentence in the module or its companion pages; *measured* is a search whose command is in *Sources*; *read* is a reading of code against specification text, not run. Nothing was built or run. Requirement 1 turns every *read* finding into a fixture before anything changes.

## Findings

The three kinds are those of `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: a **definition defect** is repaired in a definition or the binding, a **runtime gap** in this repository's libraries, a **language gap** in etalii-adp/etalii.adp. A fourth kind appears here more than in the earlier documents: a **module defect**, where today's code damages a file and the conversion would repair it by accident.

### A. The DISL definitions against the module

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | The three drafts are DISL 0.1. The client's `parseDisl` refuses anything but 0.3. Each is rewritten at 0.3 before it can be bundled. | Definition defect | Read |
| A2 | The companion pages list as inexpressible what DISL 0.2 and 0.3 answer, and the excerpt in `specifications/disl/` already shows most of it: a simulated run (`simulate`, 9.6), one menu entry per dependency (`forEach`, 7.3), a confirmation that counts and is skipped at zero (Confirmation `count` and `when`, 9.5), a finding on the second and later holder of a key (`forEach` with `positionIn`), the tool's own codes (`code` in place of `x-adp-ruleId`), line locations, the stored forms `run-job` and `for-each` of an enum value (4.5), and a derived id for an edge. The drafts still work around each. | Definition defect | Read |
| A3 | `persistence` names the plugin `net.etalii.adp.databricks.files`. It becomes `format: "fbl"` with `binding` and a `typeMap`; `files` goes, as DISL 11.2 forbids it beside a binding. | Definition defect | Read |
| A4 | The cycle rule is not `inCycle`. `DatabricksRuleSet.CycleMembers` removes every task whose dependencies are all gone and reports what remains, which is each task on a circle **and each task downstream of one**. The draft's `!self.inCycle('Dependency')` and the excerpt's `diagram.cycles` report fewer tasks. The module's set is expressible with `reachable`. | Definition defect | Read |
| A5 | `DislCelLibrary` declares none of `inCycle`, `reachable`, `successors`, `predecessors`, `diagram.cycles`, and refuses a definition that calls one. A4 needs two of them. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A6 | `simulate` is not implemented by either library: the backend knows only the context name `simulation`, and the client's canvas library has no reader for it. The three mock actions stay `useSimulatedRun.ts` until it is. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A7 | **Findings belong to the file, not to the reading.** `DatabricksValidator` parses the file under all three readings and reports the jobs' findings, then the bundle's, then the pipelines', whichever tool type asked and whatever `resource:` the registration names; its remarks say so. Three definitions each evaluate their own constraints over their own reading, so a `databricks.yml` opened as a pipeline would lose `databricks.no-default-target`, and a job file would lose the findings of every job but the selected one. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q3) | Read |
| A8 | **The order of findings.** For a job the module reports per task: the missing key, then each missing upstream, then the missing cluster, and only then moves to the next task. DISL 8.6 orders by rule in array order and, within a rule, by model order; nothing interleaves three rules per element. | Language gap, or a change to rule on (Q3) | Read |
| A9 | **A missing upstream task is a drawn, movable node.** `depends_on` naming no task draws a stub `task:<key>` with `Unresolved`, one for all tasks that name it, with the edge, and its position is stored. DISL's stub is a relation without a *target*, drawn as a line; under `typeMap` an end that names nothing leaves the relation undrawn. The written key reaches a finding as `detail.missingId` and nothing else, so no derived node type can be built from it. | Language gap | Read |
| A10 | **Elements the file has no entry for.** The bundle reading always draws a `bundle` node, labelled `bundle`, when the file has no `bundle:` key, is empty or does not parse; the pipeline reading always draws `target` and `compute`, and `notifications` when there is one. They carry stored positions under fixed ids. DISL derives elements (4.11); whether a derived element may exist while its source entry does not, and keep a stored position, is not stated. | Language gap, to confirm in design | Read |
| A11 | **A fresh key.** A dropped task is `<type>_<n>` with the first `n` no task uses. The draft counts tasks of the type and adds one, which collides after a removal. `persistence.ids.suffix` appends to a taken id and does not make the first one `_1`. CEL has no range to search. | Language gap | Read |
| A12 | **Wire ids that carry a value.** `databricks.disconnect:<key>`, `databricks.add-task:<type>`, `databricks.add-resource:<kind>`, `databricks.add-library:<kind>` and the property `databricks.pipeline:<key>` hold an argument in the id, and a target's two rows reuse `databricks.task-key` and `databricks.task-type`. Wire ids stay an `x-` block (ruled 2026-10-06); whether the derivations map a `forEach` entry to an id built from its item is the design's to check. | Runtime gap, to confirm | Read |
| A13 | The dialog refuses a task key that any job of the file uses; the writer refuses only one the task's own job uses. A definition sees one job. | Behaviour change, minor (Q4) | Read |
| A14 | `bundle-disl.sh` copies `definitions/diagrams/<module>.dis`, one definition named for the module folder. This module needs three, none named `databricks`. | Tooling, this repository | Read |
| A15 | The three layouts (longest-path columns with a cluster band, the bundle's bands, the pipeline's flow), the viewport filter and the `.proto` payloads are the host's and stay code. Not a gap: DISL names a layout as a plugin (D.2, open question 9). | None | Read |

### B. The FBL binding against the module's readers and writers

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **One body, three readings, and no binding that serves them.** FBL 9.2: every reading of a body uses the same binding, and a tool type that names another is opened read-only. Today's two bindings would make the second registration of the lakehouse example read-only. One binding for the three is therefore required, and then FBL 5.1 bites: an entry becomes at most one element, yet `resources.pipelines.<key>` is a `Resource` to the bundle and the `Pipeline` to the pipeline reading, and `resources.jobs.<key>` is a `Resource` to one and the diagram itself to another. DISL's `typeMap` answers the naming, because it is per definition: the binding reads format-named types and each definition maps them. It does not answer the rest: a type of another reading can only be hidden as `as: "header"`, which is not what a header is. | Language gap | Read |
| B2 | **The `resource` header.** `registration.resource.capture` is one capture name for the whole binding. This file needs `job` for one reading, `pipeline` for another and none for the bundle, which must see every resource. The library also selects the first value when no header is given, so under one capture the bundle would draw one pipeline. FBL 9.1 further keeps one model per open body, while two job registrations of one file select different jobs. The recorded divergence is the small end of this: `databricks.pipeline.adp` selects `bronze_to_gold` in the bundle file and `databricks-pipeline.fbl` "reads a pipeline settings document from its root and declares no registration.resource capture". | Language gap | Recorded (`settings`, `registration-resource`, both copies of the example), and read |
| B3 | **The module itself honours the header only on the canvas.** `DatabricksSession` picks the named resource; the two context providers and three commands take `entry.Jobs.FirstOrDefault()` or `entry.Pipelines.FirstOrDefault()`, and `ContextTarget` carries no registration. In a file with two pipelines, the second one's property rows show and edit the first. | Module defect | Read |
| B4 | **Typed scalars.** The module keeps every scalar as text: a task key `01`, a bundle named `2024` or `null`, an outcome written `true` without quotes. FBL types a plain YAML scalar by the core schema. This is the timeline's finding B1 and blocks this conversion equally. It is sharper here because the file belongs to another tool: `num_workers: ${var.workers}` reads as 0 workers today and `serverless: ${var.serverless}` as false, where FBL 7.4 makes a value that does not convert an unreadable entry, so the cluster or the whole pipeline would not be drawn. `DatabricksYaml.Flag` also reads `"true"` and `True` as true. | Language gap | Read; the timeline's is recorded |
| B5 | **Anchors, aliases and merge keys.** YamlDotNet's tree resolves an alias to the anchored node and does not apply `<<`. So a cluster written with a merge key shows no version or node type today, where FBL reads the merged values; and a task list shared by an alias is edited at the anchor today, changing both jobs, where FBL 4.3 makes it read-only. No fixture or example holds an anchor, an alias or a merge key. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4), and a module defect | Read; the absence is measured |
| B6 | **A key written twice** makes the file unavailable today (YamlDotNet refuses it). FBL 7.4 binds the first and reports `fbl.duplicate-key`. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4) | Read |
| B7 | **The unreadable file.** Its sentence is "This is not configuration that can be read: " followed by YamlDotNet's own message, under `databricks.unparseable`. Another parser cannot produce that tail. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4) | Read |
| B8 | **A changed value is a rewritten line.** Every writer replaces the line from its first colon: a trailing comment and the author's quotes are lost. FBL replaces the value's span in its own style. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B9 | **Values written raw.** A renamed task key, a `run_if` and a cluster key are written without quoting, and `Quote` does not quote `yes`, `null`, `123`, or a leading `*`, `&`, `!`, `%`, `@`. A `run_if` of `[x` is written, the file stops parsing, and every edit is withheld until undo. A new job's `name:` is the base name unquoted. FBL's plain-safe rule quotes each. | Module defect | Read |
| B10 | **Keys found by their text.** `FindKey` takes the first line in an entry's range that starts with the key, at any depth, so a `for_each_task` written before its task's own `task_key` has its inner key renamed. A key that is absent is inserted directly after the entry's first line at the indentation of the line after that, which puts `run_if` inside `notebook_task` when that mapping comes first. | Module defect | Read |
| B11 | **Where a new key goes.** `run_if`, `job_cluster_key` and `depends_on` go directly under the task's first line. FBL puts a key where the rule's `keys` order gives, and a created `depends_on` after `task_key`. They agree on the fixture and differ for a task that already has `depends_on`. A new resource kind goes directly under `resources:` today and at the end of that container in FBL. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B12 | **Flow collections.** `tasks: []`, `depends_on: [{task_key: a}]` and a JSON `libraries` array written on one line are appended to as if they were block lists: the first two write a broken file, and removing a library from a one-line array removes the whole line. FBL's `json` family handles the one-line array; for YAML a flow collection's only writable span is the whole collection, which is the timeline's finding B4. | Module defect, and a language gap | Read |
| B13 | **Leading comments.** A removed task leaves the comment lines above it; FBL's line span takes them with the entry. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B14 | **The example binding reads task types the tool does not have.** Its `type` expression strips `_task`, giving `spark_python`, `python_wheel`, `run_job`, `spark_jar` and `for_each` where the module gives `python`, `wheel`, `run-job`, `jar` and `for-each`. It binds no `source`, drops a task without `task_key` (`when: has(entry.task_key)`) where the module reports `databricks.task-key-missing`, and its relation rule drops a dependency whose upstream is missing, where the hype cycle's pattern (an element with reference attributes) keeps it. | Definition defect | Read |
| B15 | **Ids.** Layout keys are `task:<key>`, `cluster:<key>`, `resource:<kind>/<key>`, `unknown:<path>`, `target:<name>`, `library:<path>` and the fixed `bundle`, `pipeline`, `target`, `compute`, `notifications`. Natural ids join with a bar, not `/`, and the default id pattern admits neither `/` nor `$`, `{` or `*`, which a library path such as `transformations/gold/**` holds. Two libraries of one path and different kinds share an id, as do all libraries of kind `other`, and the writer allows the first. | Definition defect, and a module defect | Read; `other` is recorded in the companion page |
| B16 | **A rename drops the position.** The layout entry of `task:old` goes stale and is pruned. FBL 8.4 moves it in the same edit, in both files, undone together. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q5) | Recorded (companion page); FBL's side read |
| B17 | **Skeletons and nested containers.** A dropped task's skeleton depends on its type (three reachable, seven in the writer); `insert.skeleton` is one text per rule, and FBL does not say which of several rules of one type plans an add. Adding a resource to a file without `resources:` creates two containers at once; `insert.create` is one. A YAML library is a nested mapping whose `kind` and `path` the example binds by expression, which the one-place rule makes unwritable; its `emit` covers JSON only. | Language gap, to settle by fixture | Read |
| B18 | **Schema or target.** The pipeline's schema is read from `schema`, else from the legacy `target`, and written to `schema`. `override` is the reverse: the second slot wins on read and is removed on write. | Language gap, minor | Read |
| B19 | **Refusal sentences.** The module's are its own ("The job has no tasks section to add into."). The planner's are the library's, built from type names. One coincides only by the binding's name: `The {binding} file has no "catalog" to rewrite.` reads as today's sentence for a binding called `settings`. | Language gap | Measured |
| B20 | **The template.** The factory's key is lowercased; FBL's `{key}` placeholder is not, and prefixes `_` before a digit. The example templates write `./main.ipynb` and a name of `{base}`; the factory writes `notebooks/<key>` and, for a pipeline, the key. The three new documents are one binding's `template.byOrigin`. | Language gap, and a definition defect | Read |
| B21 | **Lenient header reading.** `DatabricksHeaders` reads `resource:` in any case, without a space after the colon, in the first eight lines. FBL 8.1 separates on the first colon and space. | Definition defect or none, to settle by fixture | Read |
| B22 | **Family order.** JSON is YAML, so a settings file read under `yaml` is one flow collection and unwritable. The binding must say `family: "json"` with `alsoRead: ["yaml"]`, also for the bundle file. | Definition defect | Read |

### C. Language gaps, as they would be reported to etalii-adp/etalii.adp

1. **FBL: several readings with different metamodels over one binding** (B1). Candidates: a rule's `readings` listing the origins it is read for; or `typeMap` gaining `as: "none"`; or 9.2 relaxed to bindings of one FBL document that declare each other as compatible.
2. **FBL: a resource capture per reading** (B2), and what one open body's model is when two readings select different resources. Candidate: `registration.resource` as a map from origin to capture.
3. **FBL: a YAML scalar as written** (B4), the timeline's first gap, with the addition that a value which does not convert must not cost the element when the file is another tool's.
4. **FBL: opening an empty or one-line flow collection** (B12), the timeline's second gap.
5. **FBL: a refusal's sentence** (B19). Candidate: a text beside `empty: "refuse"`, `absent` and a missing container, as `readOnly` already takes one.
6. **FBL: which rule plans an add when several share a type; two containers created by one insert; a nested mapping written for a YAML sequence item** (B17).
7. **FBL: a fallback slot read when the first is absent** (B18), and **a lowercased key placeholder** (B20).
8. **DISL: a placeholder node for a reference that names nothing** (A9), and **an element with no entry of its own that keeps a stored position** (A10).
9. **DISL: the order of findings across rules** (A8), and **the first free name of a pattern** (A11).

Gaps 1, 2 and 3 block the FBL half. Requirement 10 says they are reported with their evidence and never worked around silently.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | When an edit changes one value, adds one key or removes one entry, what is written? | **(default) What FBL writes**: the value's span in its own style, a new key where the binding orders it, an entry with its leading comments; the transcript's edit hunks are regenerated once and reviewed as a diff. · **What the writers write today**: the transcript stays byte-identical and FBL needs a whole-line rewrite and a key's place after the first line, a language change first. · Other. | 6.2, 6.3, 1.4 |
| Q2 | Gaps 1 to 3 block reading the body through a binding. What happens meanwhile? | **(default) Two stages**: the definitions, the derivation and the client now, with the DISL model built from the module's own readers as the timeline's is; the binding when FBL has the constructs. · **Work around them**: module code selects the resource, hides the other readings' types and reads scalars as text, each named as standing in for a gap. · **Wait** with all of it. · Other. | 4, 5, 6 |
| Q3 | Findings are the file's today, in the module's own order (A7, A8). | **(default) As today**: every finding of the file, in today's order, whichever reading asked, by module code that joins the three definitions' findings and is named as standing in for gap 9. · **Per reading**: each tool type reports its own, in DISL's order, named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 3.3 |
| Q4 | Readings and findings the languages would change (merge keys read, a duplicate key tolerated, the parser's message, the dialog's wider key check, `fbl.stale-view-data`, `fbl.unknown-header`). | **(default) Switched off or kept as today in this conversion**, each raised afterwards as a small change of its own. · **Adopted now**, each named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 3.3, 4.4 |
| Q5 | The module defects found (B3, B9, B10, B12, B15) and the position lost on a rename (B16). | **(default) Repaired on purpose**, each with a guard seen to fail against today's code first, because each damages a file or edits the wrong element. · **Reproduced**, so the transcript stays identical, and repaired later. · Other. | 5.3, 6.4, 6.6 |
| Q6 | Is the client in scope? | **(default) Yes**: the canvas is compiled from the three bundled definitions with `compileNotation`, today's hand-written one kept in a test as the oracle. · **No**: backend only. · Other. | 8 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product direction (2026-09-26) is one definition per tool, interpreted by a core in each IDE. Databricks is the first tool of the series whose file ADP does not own and the first whose body is read three ways. `product.md`'s *Don't reinvent, integrate* is this tool's whole premise: the file stays Databricks' and ADP adds nothing to it. What the conversion finds about FBL section 9 is owed to the C4 and W3C tool types, which lean on the same section, before they are converted.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: An oracle before any change

**User Story:** As the owner of the tool, I want what it answers today frozen before anything is converted, so that every later step is held to it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN a parity transcript `Parity/databricks.transcript.json` SHALL be generated from today's hand-written code and committed before any provider, reader or writer is changed: per document and per reading, the context menu of every element, of a placement, of a connect gesture and of an unknown id; the property rows; the findings; every mapped payload; and a scripted edit sequence with each step's answer and the hunks it made.
2. The corpus SHALL be the 11 fixtures, the `examples/lakehouse` files and their copies under `src/examples/`, and **one new fixture for each finding marked Read** in tables A and B, written so that the finding shows in the transcript or is struck from this document with the reason. Among them SHALL be a file with two jobs and two pipelines, a file with an anchor, an alias and a merge key, a file whose typed positions hold `${var.x}`, and a settings file written on one line.
3. A test SHALL require today's code to reproduce the transcript byte for byte, and SHALL have been seen to fail against a deliberately changed sentence first.
4. WHEN a later step changes the transcript THEN the change SHALL be one this document names (Q1, Q3, Q4, Q5), regenerated on purpose, with the diff of the checked-in file as its review.
5. `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` SHALL compare the ids per type that the bindings read with those `JobParser`, `PipelineParser` and `BundleParser` read, for every Databricks file of the real-file corpus.

### Requirement 2: Three definitions, at DISL 0.3, bundled

**User Story:** As a tool engineer, I want one definition per Databricks tool type that every host runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `databricks-bundle.dis`, `databricks-job.dis` and `databricks-pipeline.dis` in etalii-adp/etalii.adp SHALL be rewritten at DISL 0.3 with the constructs of finding A2, the cycle rule of A4, and an `x-databricks` block each mapping tools, actions and properties to today's wire ids (A12), and SHALL validate against the DISL schema there.
2. Their companion pages SHALL say what DISL 0.3 cannot express, which is findings A8 to A11 and whatever Requirement 10 adds, and nothing that 0.3 can.
3. The three SHALL be bundled into `src/diagrams/databricks/definition/` by `bundle-disl.sh`, extended to bundle a named definition into a module whose folder has another name (A14), each with its provenance, embedded in the backend project and held by a `BundledDefinition.Tests`.
4. WHEN each bundled definition is loaded by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` THEN it SHALL load with no diagnostic of severity error.

### Requirement 3: Toolbox, menus, rows and findings are derived

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the palettes, menus, property rows and findings to come from the definitions.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The three toolboxes, the context menu of every target, the property rows, the removal confirmation and every read-only reason SHALL be derived through `ToolboxDerivation`, `ContextMenuDerivation` and `FormDerivation`, mapped to the wire ids of `x-databricks`, and the providers SHALL compute none themselves.
2. Every sentence a user reads today SHALL be read unchanged: "Disconnect from 'ingest'" once per upstream, "Removing this task also removes the 1 dependency touching it." and its plural, asked only when a dependency goes, the three "(simulated)" entries, and the two rows every selection wears, "Workspace connection" and "Last simulated run".
3. The eleven findings SHALL keep their codes (`databricks.task-key-missing` to `databricks.schema-without-catalog`, and `databricks.unparseable`), severities, sentences and line locations; they SHALL be reported for the file and in today's order (Q3); and no finding the tool does not give today SHALL appear (Q4).
4. WHEN the derived answers are compared with the transcript THEN menus, rows, findings and payloads SHALL be byte-identical for every reading of every document.
5. The hand-written providers' logic SHALL be kept in the test project as the oracle and removed from the product code.

### Requirement 4: One binding, three readings

**User Story:** As a user, I want every file that opens today to open the same, as a bundle, a job or a pipeline, from one binding.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL own one FBL document, `backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Databricks/databricks.fbl`, with one binding that the three definitions name, each with its own `typeMap` (B1). The two examples in etalii.adp SHALL be brought in line with it or the difference recorded.
2. WHEN two registrations open one body as different tool types THEN both SHALL be editable, an edit in one SHALL show in the other without a reload, and one undo history SHALL serve both.
3. The elements each reading reads SHALL be those its parser reads today, for every document of the corpus: the unmodelled root keys and resource kinds as `Unknown`, a task without a key reported and not drawn, a dependency on a missing task kept, drawn with its stub and reported (A9, B14), a bare settings file recognised by `name` or `libraries` only where the file has no `resources.pipelines`.
4. Every value SHALL be read as the text it was written with, and a value that does not convert (B4) SHALL NOT remove its element; anchors, aliases, merge keys and a repeated key SHALL read as the user has ruled (Q4).
5. A body that is not YAML or JSON SHALL open with `databricks.unparseable` and every edit withheld with "This file does not parse, so nothing can be edited until it is fixed."
6. The binding SHALL read a JSON body under the `json` family and a YAML body under `yaml` (B22), and SHALL declare the three new documents as `template.byOrigin`, each byte-identical to what `DatabricksDocumentFactory` writes today for the corpus of base names in its tests (B20).

### Requirement 5: The `resource` header and the registration

**User Story:** As an author of a file that declares several resources, I want each registration to show and edit the one it names.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. A job registration SHALL select by job key and a pipeline registration by pipeline key, each from its `resource:` header and the first in document order without one; a bundle registration SHALL select nothing (B2). The `registration-resource` entries of `RealFiles/divergences.json` SHALL be removed because they no longer occur.
2. Two registrations of one file that name different resources SHALL each show their own.
3. Menus, property rows, drops and commands SHALL act on the resource the registration names, with a test seen to fail against today's providers first (B3, Q5).
4. Every position stored in a registration today SHALL be applied after the conversion with no registration rewritten: the definition's id strategy SHALL yield today's ids (B15).
5. A move SHALL write only the registration, through the library's registration writer, as one undo step; a document opened without a registration SHALL refuse it with today's sentence.

### Requirement 6: Every edit is written by splices

**User Story:** As a user of a file Databricks' tooling also reads, I want an edit to change what I changed and to leave the file valid.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every command SHALL write through `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` as a model change planned into splices; no module code SHALL build a line of YAML or JSON, and `DatabricksSplices` SHALL leave the product code.
2. WHEN a value changes THEN only its span SHALL change, in its own style (Q1): a trailing comment and the author's quotes SHALL survive.
3. A new key, a new entry and a created container SHALL go where the binding declares (Q1), in the indentation the file already uses, and the JSON forms SHALL keep their separators as today.
4. A value SHALL be written so that it reads back as the same text (B9); an edit SHALL never be written that leaves the body unreadable (B12), and where FBL cannot make it the edit SHALL be refused with a sentence.
5. Renaming a task SHALL rewrite its key and every `depends_on` reference in one edit; removing a task SHALL remove every dependency that touches it, and a `depends_on` key left empty, in one undo step.
6. A rename SHALL carry the task's stored position with it (B16, Q5).
7. Every refusal SHALL keep today's sentence (B19); WHERE FBL gives its own THEN the sentence SHALL come from the definition's check before the plan, or from module code named as standing in for gap 5.
8. Undo SHALL restore the body byte for byte, and a document ADP did not change SHALL be written back byte-identical, the line-ending fixtures and the one without a final newline included.

### Requirement 7: What stays code, and why

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want what remains in the module to be what the languages cannot state.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL keep the three layouts, the element mapper and the viewport filter, the session and the document store, the `.proto` payloads, and the stand-ins this document names (Q2, Q3, Requirement 6.7).
2. The three parsers, the three writers, `DatabricksSplices`, `DatabricksHeaders`, `DatabricksRuleSet` and the logic of the three providers SHALL leave the product code once the stage that replaces each is complete (Q2).
3. WHEN the conversion is complete THEN the companion pages SHALL list every remaining module class beside the gap or host concern that keeps it.

### Requirement 8: The client

**User Story:** As a user, I want the three canvases to look and behave as they do, drawn from the definitions.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The canvas definitions SHALL be compiled from the bundled definitions with `parseDisl` and `compileNotation` (Q6); today's `DatabricksCanvas.tsx` SHALL be kept in a test as the oracle.
2. The mock run, deploy and update SHALL be the definitions' `simulate` once the canvas library plays one (A6); until then `useSimulatedRun.ts` stays, named as standing in for a runtime gap. A simulated action SHALL never reach a file or the history.
3. A `tests.md` entry SHALL cover in a real browser, in both themes: the three readings of the lakehouse example, the same file open twice with an edit in one showing in the other, a drop of each toolbox entry, a dependency drawn and removed, a missing task's stub, an outcome edge's colour, the target frames and override edges, and each simulated action.

### Requirement 9: The library work this tool needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared libraries, I want each thing this tool needs added once, for every tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` SHALL implement the graph functions the rewritten definitions call (A5) and whatever of finding A2 the derivations lack, each proven by a library test seen to fail first.
2. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` SHALL implement what FBL gains for gaps 1 to 4, each with a conformance fixture vendored from etalii.adp; a language gap SHALL NOT be repaired here.
3. No module name SHALL appear in a library change.

### Requirement 10: Gaps are recorded and reported, never tuned away

**User Story:** As the owner of DISL and FBL, I want every place the languages fall short reported with its evidence.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every language gap of section C, and any the implementation adds, SHALL be recorded in the companion pages with the construct, the fixture that shows it, and what would resolve it.
2. A gap SHALL NOT be closed by weakening a check, skipping a fixture, or stating in a definition or the binding something the tool does not do.
3. The delivery report SHALL list every gap as a candidate change for etalii-adp/etalii.adp, every definition defect repaired and every module defect repaired.
4. WHEN a *read* finding turns out not to occur THEN it SHALL be struck here with the fixture that shows it, as a small amendment.

### Requirement 11: Documentation, catalog and gates

**User Story:** As a reader of the repository, I want its pages to stay true.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/diagrams/readme.md`, `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md`, `docs/diagram-module-client-api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/solution-structure.md` SHALL be updated in the change that makes a sentence of theirs false, and the three Databricks rows of `docs/tools.md` SHALL name this specification.
2. All four gates SHALL exit zero on every pull request, judged by captured exit codes, with a newly created worktree built before a green gate is trusted about a bundled definition.
3. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets, and two traces SHALL be read back to their artefacts.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module ends as three definitions, one binding and the code Requirement 7.1 names. The house rules of `src/.editorconfig` and the three rules the gates refuse apply. The fixtures stay `-text` by their narrow glob, and the module's `.fbl` and `.dis` follow what the hype cycle's have.

### Performance

- Opening, validating and editing the largest file of the corpus SHALL not be perceptibly slower than today. A body open under several readings SHALL be read once per change.

### Reliability

- No file that opens today opens differently, unless this document names it. No edit leaves a file Databricks' tooling cannot read. An unchanged document is written back byte-identical. Every test written for a finding is seen to fail against it first.

### Usability

- Every sentence a user reads today is read unchanged, unless this document names the change.

## Out of scope

- Following `include:` globs, so that a bundle shows resources declared in other files. FBL's folder subjects could carry it; it is a new capability and its own specification.
- What the original `databricks-diagrams` specification asked for and the tool does not do, listed under *Gaps* in the three companion pages, and the Add flow's suggestion of a type from a file's content.
- Changing DISL or FBL. Gaps are reported (Requirement 10).
- The other tools of the series.

A draft against FBL 0.2, one binding for the three readings, trimmed to the rules that carry a finding; the targets, includes, variables and unmodelled keys follow the same shapes. Unsettled, and the design's to close with fixtures: the task skeleton is the notebook's only, and the Python and condition skeletons need rules of their own or a construct (B17); the `file` and `glob` libraries of a keyed pipeline are rules like `notebookLibrary`; whether a new YAML item is written as a nested mapping from a `child` slot (B17); whether `/libraries/*` must be told that the root is a settings file; the `{key}` of the templates is not the factory's lowercased key (B20); and the missing-task stub and the always-present nodes have no rule, because they are findings A9 and A10.

## Appendix: the job definition's persistence and wire ids, as drafted

The bundle and pipeline definitions differ in their `typeMap` only as the comment after the block says.

```json
{
  "persistence": {
    "format": "fbl",
    "binding": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp.ide.standalone/develop/src/diagrams/databricks/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Databricks/databricks.fbl#configuration",
    "ids": {
      "strategy": "natural", "stable": false,
      "prefix": { "Task": "task:", "JobCluster": "cluster:" },
      "pattern": "^[^\\r\\n]{1,512}$",
      "types": { "Dependency": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'edge:' + self.source.key + '->' + self.target.key" } }
    },
    "view": { "store": ["bounds"] },
    "typeMap": {
      "JobResource": { "as": "diagram", "attributes": { "key": "jobKey" } },
      "Task": { "as": "Task", "hostAttributes": ["storedKey"] },
      "JobCluster": { "as": "JobCluster" },
      "DependsOn": { "as": "Dependency", "attributes": { "from": "source", "to": "target" } },

    }
  },

    },
    "actions": {
      "renameTask": "databricks.rename-task", "setRunIf": "databricks.set-run-if", "assignCluster": "databricks.assign-cluster",
      "disconnect": "databricks.disconnect:{item.source.key}",
      "Task/delete": "databricks.remove-task", "Dependency/delete": "databricks.remove-edge", "connect": "databricks.connect",
      "simulateRun": "databricks.simulated.run-job"
    },
    "properties": {
      "key": "databricks.task-key", "type": "databricks.task-type", "source": "databricks.task-source",
      "runIf": "databricks.run-if", "clusterKey": "databricks.cluster",

```

The three `as: "header"` entries are finding B1 made visible: they hide another reading's types and are not headers. The bundle's map turns `JobResource` and `PipelineResource` into `Resource`, and the pipeline's turns `PipelineResource` into `Pipeline`. The id of a dependency whose source names nothing has no `self.source` to read, which the design must settle with finding A9. The `{item.source.key}` in an action id is finding A12 and is not a convention the derivations have today.
